Foreword · 序（Foreword）

I have always been endlessly fascinated with the details of how Google does things. I have grilled my Googler friends for information about the way things really work inside of the company. How do they manage such a massive, monolithic code repository without falling over? How do tens of thousands of engineers successfully collaborate on thousands of projects? How do they maintain the quality of their systems? Working with former Googlers has only increased my curiosity. If you’ve ever worked with a former Google engineer (or “Xoogler,” as they’re sometimes called), you’ve no doubt heard the phrase “at Google we…” Coming out of Google into other companies seems to be a shocking experience, at least from the engineering side of things. As far as this outsider can tell, the systems and processes for writing code at Google must be among the best in the world, given both the scale of the company and how often people sing their praises.

我一直对 Google 究竟是如何做事的细节充满无尽的好奇。我曾反复追问在 Google 工作的朋友，打听公司内部真实的运作方式。他们是如何管理如此庞大、单一的代码仓库而不崩溃的？数以万计的工程师是如何在成千上万个项目上成功协作的？他们又是如何维持系统质量的？与前 Google 员工共事只会让我更加好奇。如果你曾经和一位前 Google 工程师（有时被称作“Xoogler”）共事过，你一定听过那句话：“在 Google，我们……”从 Google 走到其他公司，至少在工程这一面，往往是一种令人震惊的体验。在我这个外人看来，无论从公司规模还是从人们交口称赞的频率来看，Google 编写代码的体系与流程都堪称世界顶尖之列。

In Software Engineering at Google, a set of Googlers (and some Xooglers) gives us a lengthy blueprint for many of the practices, tools, and even cultural elements that underlie software engineering at Google. It’s easy to overfocus on the amazing tools that Google has built to support writing code, and this book provides a lot of details about those tools. But it also goes beyond simply describing the tooling to give us the philosophy and processes that the teams at Google follow. These can be adapted to fit a variety of circumstances, whether or not you have the scale and tooling. To my delight, there are several chapters that go deep on various aspects of automated testing, a topic that continues to meet with too much resistance in our industry.

在《Software Engineering at Google》一书中，一群 Google 员工（以及一些 Xoogler）为我们提供了一份详尽的蓝图，勾勒出支撑 Google 软件工程的诸多实践、工具乃至文化要素。人们很容易过度聚焦于 Google 为支撑写代码而打造的那些惊艳工具，本书也确实详细介绍了这些工具。但它不止于描述工具，还向我们传递了 Google 各团队所遵循的理念与流程。无论你是否拥有 Google 那样的规模与工具，这些都可以根据各种情况加以改造适用。令我欣喜的是，有好几章深入探讨了自动化测试的方方面面——而在我们这个行业，这个话题至今仍遭遇过多的抵触。

The great thing about tech is that there is never only one way to do something. Instead, there is a series of trade-offs we all must make depending on the circumstances of our team and situation. What can we cheaply take from open source? What can our team build? What makes sense to support for our scale? When I was grilling my Googler friends, I wanted to hear about the world at the extreme end of scale: resource rich, in both talent and money, with high demands on the software being built. This anecdotal information gave me ideas on some options that I might not otherwise have considered.

科技领域最棒的一点在于：做一件事从来不止一种方法。相反，我们都必须根据团队与处境做出一系列权衡。哪些东西可以廉价地从开源中拿来就用？哪些东西该由我们团队自己构建？对于我们这样的规模，维护哪些东西才划算？我追问 Google 朋友时，想听到的是规模极端一端的世界：在人才与资金上都资源充沛，对所构建的软件又有着极高的要求。这些零散的见闻让我想到了一些原本不会考虑的选项。

With this book, we’ve written down those options for everyone to read. Of course, Google is a unique company, and it would be foolish to assume that the right way to run your software engineering organization is to precisely copy their formula. Applied practically, this book will give you ideas on how things could be done, and a lot of information that you can use to bolster your arguments for adopting best practices like testing, knowledge sharing, and building collaborative teams.

通过这本书，我们把这些选项写下来供所有人阅读。当然，Google 是一家独特的公司，若以为照搬它的配方就是运营你自己软件工程组织的正确方式，那是愚蠢的。落到实践中，本书会给你提供“事情可以怎么做”的思路，以及大量可用来支撑你论据的信息，帮助你去推行测试、知识共享、构建协作团队等最佳实践。

You may never need to build Google yourself, and you may not even want to reach for the same techniques they apply in your organization. But if you aren’t familiar with the practices Google has developed, you’re missing a perspective on software engineering that comes from tens of thousands of engineers working collaboratively on software over the course of more than two decades. That knowledge is far too valuable to ignore.

你也许永远不需要自己去“建造一个 Google”，甚至未必想在自己的组织里套用他们用的那些技术。但如果你不了解 Google 沉淀下来的这些实践，你就错失了一种软件工程的视角——它来自数万工程师二十多年来协作开发软件的经验。这份知识太过宝贵，不容忽略。

— Camille Fournier, Author, The Manager’s Path

—— Camille Fournier，《管理之道》（The Manager’s Path）作者

Preface · 前言（Preface）

This book is titled Software Engineering at Google. What precisely do we mean by software engineering? What distinguishes “software engineering” from “programming” or “computer science”? And why would Google have a unique perspective to add to the corpus of previous software engineering literature written over the past 50 years?

本书名为《Software Engineering at Google》。我们所说的“软件工程”究竟指什么？“软件工程”与“编程”或“计算机科学”有何区别？在过去 50 年汗牛充栋的软件工程文献之上，Google 又凭什么能贡献出一套独特的视角？

The terms “programming” and “software engineering” have been used interchangeably for quite some time in our industry, although each term has a different emphasis and different implications. University students tend to study computer science and get jobs writing code as “programmers.”

在我们这个行业里，“编程”与“软件工程”这两个词在相当长时间里被混用，尽管各自侧重点与隐含意味并不相同。大学生们通常学习计算机科学，毕业后以“程序员”的身份写代码谋生。

“Software engineering,” however, sounds more serious, as if it implies the application of some theoretical knowledge to build something real and precise. Mechanical engineers, civil engineers, aeronautical engineers, and those in other engineering disciplines all practice engineering. They all work in the real world and use the application of their theoretical knowledge to create something real. Software engineers also create “something real,” though it is less tangible than the things other engineers create.

然而，“软件工程”听起来更严肃，仿佛意味着把某种理论知识应用起来，去构建真实而精确的东西。机械工程师、土木工程师、航空工程师以及其他工程学科的人都在做工程。他们都在现实世界中工作，运用理论知识的实践去创造真实之物。软件工程师也在创造“真实之物”，只不过它不如其他工程师所造之物那样有形。

Unlike those more established engineering professions, current software engineering theory or practice is not nearly as rigorous. Aeronautical engineers must follow rigid guidelines and practices, because errors in their calculations can cause real damage; programming, on the whole, has traditionally not followed such rigorous practices. But, as software becomes more integrated into our lives, we must adopt and rely on more rigorous engineering methods. We hope this book helps others see a path toward more reliable software practices.

与那些成熟得多的工程职业不同，当今软件工程的理论与实践还远远谈不上严谨。航空工程师必须遵循严苛的准则与规范，因为他们计算中的错误会造成真实的损失；而总体而言，编程传统上并不遵循如此严格的做法。但是，随着软件越来越深入地融入我们的生活，我们必须采用并依赖更严谨的工程方法。我们希望本书能帮助他人看清一条通往更可靠软件实践的道路。

Programming Over Time · 随时间推移的编程

We propose that “software engineering” encompasses not just the act of writing code, but all of the tools and processes an organization uses to build and maintain that code over time. What practices can a software organization introduce that will best keep its code valuable over the long term? How can engineers make a codebase more sustainable and the software engineering discipline itself more rigorous? We don’t have fundamental answers to these questions, but we hope that Google’s collective experience over the past two decades illuminates possible paths toward finding those answers.

我们提出：“软件工程”不仅包含写代码这一动作，还包含一个组织随时间构建并维护该代码所用的全部工具与流程。一个软件组织可以引入哪些实践，才能最好地让其代码长期保持价值？工程师又如何让代码库更具可持续性、让软件工程这门学科本身更严谨？对这些问题我们没有根本性的答案，但我们希望 Google 过去二十多年的集体经验，能为寻找这些答案照亮若干可能的路径。

One key insight we share in this book is that software engineering can be thought of as “programming integrated over time.” What practices can we introduce to our code to make it sustainable—able to react to necessary change—over its life cycle, from conception to introduction to maintenance to deprecation?

本书要分享的一个关键洞见是：软件工程可以被理解为“随时间积分的编程”。我们可以为代码引入哪些实践，使其在整个生命周期里——从构思、引入、维护到弃用——都保持可持续，即能够对必要的变化做出反应？

The book emphasizes three fundamental principles that we feel software organizations should keep in mind when designing, architecting, and writing their code:

本书强调三条基本原则，我们认为软件组织在设计、架构和编写代码时应当牢记：

  • Time and Change: How code will need to adapt over the length of its life.

    时间与变化（Time and Change）：代码在其整个生命周期中将需要如何适应变化。

  • Scale and Growth: How an organization will need to adapt as it evolves.

    规模与增长（Scale and Growth）：组织在演进过程中将需要如何适应。

  • Trade-offs and Costs: How an organization makes decisions, based on the lessons of Time and Change and Scale and Growth.

    权衡与成本（Trade-offs and Costs）：组织如何基于“时间与变化”和“规模与增长”的经验教训来做决策。

Throughout the chapters, we have tried to tie back to these themes and point out ways in which such principles affect engineering practices and allow them to be sustainable. (See Chapter 1 for a full discussion.)

在各章中，我们都力求回扣这些主题，并指出这些原则以何种方式影响工程实践、并使其可持续。（完整讨论见第 1 章。）

Google’s Perspective · Google 的视角

Google has a unique perspective on the growth and evolution of a sustainable software ecosystem, stemming from our scale and longevity. We hope that the lessons we have learned will be useful as your organization evolves and embraces more sustainable practices.

凭借自身的规模与 longevity（长久历史），Google 对可持续软件生态的成长与演进有着独特视角。我们希望，当你的组织演进并拥抱更可持续的实践时，我们所学到的经验能派上用场。

We’ve divided the topics in this book into three main aspects of Google’s software engineering landscape: Culture, Processes, and Tools.

我们把本书的主题划分为 Google 软件工程图景的三大方面：文化（Culture）、流程（Processes）与工具（Tools）。

Google’s culture is unique, but the lessons we have learned in developing our engineering culture are widely applicable. Our chapters on Culture (Part II) emphasize the collective nature of a software development enterprise, that the development of software is a team effort, and that proper cultural principles are essential for an organization to grow and remain healthy.

Google 的文化是独特的，但我们在培育工程文化过程中学到的经验却具有广泛适用性。我们关于文化的章节（第二部分）强调：软件开发事业具有集体性，软件开发是团队协作的成果，而恰当的文化原则对于一个组织的成长与保持健康至关重要。

The techniques outlined in our Processes chapters (Part III) are familiar to most software engineers, but Google’s large size and long-lived codebase provides a more complete stress test for developing best practices. Within those chapters, we have tried to emphasize what we have found to work over time and at scale as well as identify areas where we don’t yet have satisfying answers.

我们流程章节（第三部分）所勾勒的技术，对大多数软件工程师来说并不陌生；但 Google 的庞大规模与长寿代码库，为打磨最佳实践提供了一场更完整的压力测试。在这些章节中，我们力求强调那些经时间与规模检验确实行之有效的做法，同时也指出那些我们尚无令人满意答案的领域。

Finally, our Tools chapters (Part IV) illustrate how we leverage our investments in tooling infrastructure to provide benefits to our codebase as it both grows and ages. In some cases, these tools are specific to Google, though we point out open source or third-party alternatives where applicable. We expect that these basic insights apply to most engineering organizations.

最后，我们的工具章节（第四部分）展示了我们如何借助在工具基础设施上的投入，让不断成长、不断老化的代码库持续受益。其中有些工具是 Google 专有的，但在适用之处我们也会指出开源或第三方的替代方案。我们相信这些基本洞见适用于大多数工程组织。

The culture, processes, and tools outlined in this book describe the lessons that a typical software engineer hopefully learns on the job. Google certainly doesn’t have a monopoly on good advice, and our experiences presented here are not intended to dictate what your organization should do. This book is our perspective, but we hope you will find it useful, either by adopting these lessons directly or by using them as a starting point when considering your own practices, specialized for your own problem domain.

本书所勾勒的文化、流程与工具，描述的是一名普通软件工程师在工作中有望学到的经验。Google 当然并不垄断好的建议，我们在此呈现的经验也无意规定你的组织该怎么做。本书是我们的视角，但我们希望它对你有用——无论是直接采纳这些经验，还是把它们作为起点，去思考你自己、针对你自身问题领域定制的实践。

Neither is this book intended to be a sermon. Google itself still imperfectly applies many of the concepts within these pages. The lessons that we have learned, we learned through our failures: we still make mistakes, implement imperfect solutions, and need to iterate toward improvement. Yet the sheer size of Google’s engineering organization ensures that there is a diversity of solutions for every problem. We hope that this book contains the best of that group.

本书也无意成为一通说教。Google 自己在践行本书中的许多概念时仍有欠缺。我们所学到的教训，是通过失败换来的：我们仍在犯错，仍在实现不完美的方案，仍需要迭代改进。然而，Google 工程组织的庞大规模确保了每个问题都有多样化的解法。我们希望本书收录的是这其中最好的那一部分。

What This Book Isn’t · 本书不涉及什么

This book is not meant to cover software design, a discipline that requires its own book (and for which much content already exists). Although there is some code in this book for illustrative purposes, the principles are language neutral, and there is little actual “programming” advice within these chapters. As a result, this text doesn’t cover many important issues in software development: project management, API design, security hardening, internationalization, user interface frameworks, or other language-specific concerns. Their omission in this book does not imply their lack of importance. Instead, we choose not to cover them here knowing that we could not provide the treatment they deserve. We have tried to make the discussions in this book more about engineering and less about programming.

本书并不打算覆盖软件设计——那是一门需要单独成书（且已有大量内容）的学科。虽然书中有一些用于说明的代码，但其中的原则是语言中立的，各章里也几乎没有真正的“编程”建议。因此，本书并未涵盖软件开发中的许多重要议题：项目管理、API 设计、安全加固、国际化、用户界面框架，以及其他与特定语言相关的问题。本书略去它们，并不意味着它们不重要。相反，我们选择不在此讨论，是因为我们知道自己无法给予它们应有的深入处理。我们努力让本书的讨论更偏向工程、而不是编程。

Parting Remarks · 临别之言

This text has been a labor of love on behalf of all who have contributed, and we hope that you receive it as it is given: as a window into how a large software engineering organization builds its products. We also hope that it is one of many voices that helps move our industry to adopt more forward-thinking and sustainable practices. Most important, we further hope that you enjoy reading it and can adopt some of its lessons to your own concerns. — Tom Manshreck

本书凝聚了所有贡献者的心血与热爱，我们也希望你能如我们所给予的那样接受它：把它当作一扇窗，窥见一个大型软件工程组织是如何构建产品的。我们也希望它成为众多声音之一，推动我们这个行业采用更具前瞻性、更可持续的实践。最重要的是，我们更希望你读得愉快，并能把其中一些经验用到你自己关切的问题上。—— Tom Manshreck

Conventions Used in This Book · 本书使用的约定

  • Italic: indicates new terms, URLs, email addresses, filenames, and file extensions.

    斜体：标示新术语、URL、电子邮箱地址、文件名与文件扩展名。

  • Constant width: used for program listings, as well as within paragraphs to refer to program elements such as variable or function names, databases, data types, environment variables, statements, and keywords.

    等宽字体：用于程序清单，以及在段落中指代程序元素，如变量名、函数名、数据库、数据类型、环境变量、语句与关键字。

  • Constant width bold: shows commands or other text that should be typed literally by the user.

    等宽粗体：显示应由用户逐字键入的命令或其他文本。

  • Constant width italic: shows text that should be replaced with user-supplied values or by values determined by context.

    等宽斜体：显示应由用户提供的值或由上下文确定的值所替换的文本。

For more than 40 years, O’Reilly Media has provided technology and business training, knowledge, and insight to help companies succeed.
